The SJC stayed all further proceedings and declined to annul the installations, finding no PCA precedent for such relief.

artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Psiaki complained that Covenant Presbyterian Church's Session erred in installing officers elected at a congregational meeting that excluded communicant members under age 18 from voting, in violation of the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint (15-5), holding that all communicant members have a constitutional right to vote in officer elections regardless of age, and that church bylaws may not override BCO provisions; multiple dissenting opinions argued that BCO 20-3 and 24-3's phrase 'good and regular standing' permits local sessions to establish reasonable minimum voting ages.

artifacts.title: Dudt v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint by an ordained Deacon whose nomination for re-election was not advanced by the Session, holding that the Session's exercise of discretion in evaluating a candidate's eligibility for office did not constitute clear error requiring reversal. The dissent argued the proper standard of review was BCO 39-3.4 (de novo for constitutional interpretation), not 39-3.3 (great deference), because the Session applied extra-biblical and extra-constitutional attendance standards in blocking re-election.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Tolivar Wills complained that Metro Atlanta Presbytery improperly dissolved Grace North Atlanta Church without following formal judicial process under BCO 40-6. artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.

artifacts.title: Inactive or non-locally-elected elders as General Assembly commissioners

matches.evidence: A rotating-session inactive elder may be elected GA commissioner, but a ruling elder never elected in that congregation may not serve as its commissioner.

artifacts.title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation

matches.evidence: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.
